what_this_is: Measured dollars spent in each pattern (cost at stake), from committed Bentham usage. Not a saving; never a Junto score. Only junto.py add-test with two measured arms verifies a saving.

waves.note: from Kean measures: coordinator share only; per-call patterns need a usage table
from Kean measures: coordinator share only; per-call patterns need a usage table

savers.what: Main sessions (Bentham's 'coordinator' rows) that do bounded work themselves, poll GitHub, or carry long turns: delegate bounded tasks to cheaper workers, wait with one background watcher, keep turns short.
savers.test: Two comparable waves on the same route (same claim-kit route, same reviewer setup): one run as before, one with the lean-coordination brief. Compare coordinator plus worker dollars per filed claim, and rejects per attempt (quality must not fall).

arms.before: a wave whose prompt does not include PROTOCOL.md (the Cujas or Haloander shape)
arms.after: the next wave on the same route whose prompt includes PROTOCOL.md

savers.matched_on: same route (Haloander h01 page check), batch size 25, same producer and reviewer models, planted controls 2 per batch, same budget cap
savers.measure: bentham.py usage --wave W --phase P --reported-costs RUN/COSTS.log per arm; units = filed claims; accepted/rejected = blind-review verdicts
savers.add_test: junto.py add-test --candidate C-20261109-1 --unit-of-work filed_claim --matched-on '<as above>' --before-usd X --before-units N --before-session S --before-accepted A --before-rejected R --after-usd Y --after-units M --after-session T --after-accepted B --after-rejected Q --test-cost-usd 0 --complete-costs

savers.what: End a long coordinator context at a phase boundary and continue in a fresh session from the handoff notes (Revere), instead of carrying hundreds of thousands of tokens into every call.
savers.test: Same wave phase run twice: once continuing the long session, once handed off to a fresh session at the phase boundary. Compare coordinator dollars per completed batch.
savers.tool: jobs/carnot-coordinator/handoff.py (context check at 300,000 tokens per call; write packet)

arms.before: batch k+1 run in the coordinator session that ran batch k (context > 300k per call)
arms.after: batch k+1 run by a fresh coordinator from handoff.py's packet

savers.matched_on: consecutive batches of one wave, same route and models, same batch size; the fresh arm's setup (reading the packet and checking out inputs) is counted in its cost
savers.measure: bentham.py usage with --session-id per arm; units = completed batches (filed or reviewed)
savers.add_test: junto.py add-test --candidate C-20261020-1 --unit-of-work completed_batch --matched-on '<as above>' --before-usd X --before-units 1 --before-session S --after-usd Y --after-units 1 --after-session T --test-cost-usd 0 --complete-costs

savers.what: Do not hold a 1-hour prompt cache across long idle waits; let it lapse or end the turn and resume.
savers.test: Two waits of the same length on the same kind of GitHub run: one holding the session, one ending the turn and resuming. Compare dollars per hour of wait.
savers.tool: jobs/carnot-coordinator/await_run.py (background, ends the turn) and handoff.py for waits over ~55 min

arms.before: a coordinator that waits on a multi-hour run in its session (checks or a held turn)
arms.after: a coordinator that writes a packet and stops; a fresh session resumes when await_run exits

savers.matched_on: the same workflow (run-jobs daily selection or a claim-kit rebuild), waits within 20% of each other in length, the same coordinator model
savers.measure: dollars from the end of dispatch to the first productive call after the run ends (cache writes and reads of the resume included), per wait hour
savers.add_test: junto.py add-test --candidate C-20261020-2 --unit-of-work wait_hour --matched-on '<as above>' --before-usd X --before-units H1 --before-session S --after-usd Y --after-units H2 --after-session T --test-cost-usd 0 --complete-costs
